    2026 Fall
    #29147
    COMPSCI 61A 001 - LEC 001 offered through Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences
    section closed

    The Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs

    Kay Ousterhout, John DeNero
    Aug 26, 2026 - Dec 11, 2026
    Mo, We, Fr
    12:00 pm - 12:59 pm
    Wheeler 150
    Class #:29147
    Units:4

    Instruction Mode: In-Person Instruction

    Time Conflict Enrollment Allowed

    Open Seats

    284 Unreserved Seats

    An introduction to programming and computer science focused on abstraction techniques as means to manage program complexity. Techniques include procedural abstraction; control abstraction using recursion, higher-order functions, generators, and streams; data abstraction using interfaces, objects, classes, and generic operators; and language abstraction using interpreters and macros. The course exposes students to programming paradigms, including functional, object-oriented, and declarative approaches. It includes an introduction to asymptotic analysis of algorithms. There are several significant programming projects.

    2026 Fall
    #34649
    COMPSCI 194 061A - LEC 061A offered through Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences
    section closed

    Special Topics

    Functional Programming and AI-Assisted Application Development
    John DeNero, Kay Ousterhout
    Aug 26, 2026 - Dec 11, 2026
    Fr
    10:00 am - 10:59 am
    Social Sciences Building 170
    Class #:34649
    Units:1

    Instruction Mode: In-Person Instruction

    Open Seats

    27 Unreserved Seats

    An introduction to functional programming, algebraic type systems, web technologies, software application design, and AI-assisted application development. Course Objectives: This course directly follows the introduction to programming and computer science provided by Computer Science 61A and Data Science C88C and prepares students to build a full application using modern tools and technologies. The learning goals of this course include: -Preparing students to learn how to use statically typed programming languages such as Java and Rust in future courses, such as CS 61B and CS 162. -Preparing students to use World Wide Web technologies in application development in future courses, such as CS 160 and CS 169. -Preparing students to extend their understanding of programming languages and programming tools in future courses, such as CS 164. -Gain experience with AI-assisted programming.
